Compile a type into a staged JSON decoder node (#850). A node is a Coder whose decode function takes a resolver for named types (see jsonCoder) paired with a JSON value; its encode function is unused. Nodes are data rather than bare functions so that no host's eta expansion can move the compile-time work under the decoding lambda. All schema work (annotation stripping, type-application reduction, field and variant tables) happens once here rather than at every node of every decoded value, while every error is still reported at decode time, exactly as fromJson reports it.

Decode a JSON value to a Hydra term given a type and type name. Returns Left for type mismatches. The compactMaps flag mirrors toJson's: it must be False for any caller reading the checked-in dist/json module-bootstrapping representation, since a byte-stable published-host decoder must be able to read that data unmodified.

Build a staged JSON coder for a type (#850). Its decode function is equivalent to fromJson applied to the same arguments, and its encode function to toJson, but the schema is compiled once when the coder is built, so a caller that keeps the coder and applies it to many values does not re-interpret the schema for each one. Each named type reachable from the given type is compiled exactly once, and named-type references go through a recursive local function rather than a recursive value, so no host needs lazy let-bindings.
